content.title: WHY YOUR 'HEALTHY' MORNING ROUTINE MIGHT BE {{BACKFIRING}}
facts: **Squeezed orange juice with breakfast** -> the vitamin C is real, but the sugar hits your blood just as fast as soda, spiking insulin before you've even started your day.
**Stretching cold muscles first thing** -> without a few minutes of light movement first, static stretching on stiff joints can strain tendons instead of loosening them.
**Weighing yourself every morning** -> daily fluctuations from water and sodium can swing 1-2 kg, tricking your brain into stress responses over numbers that mean nothing.
**Skipping breakfast for 'intermittent fasting'** -> if you train hard in the morning, going too long without fuel can push your body to break down muscle for energy instead of fat.
**Taking a multivitamin on an empty stomach** -> fat-soluble vitamins like A, D, E and K need dietary fat to absorb properly, so without food most of it just passes through.
**Using mouthwash right after brushing** -> it rinses away the concentrated fluoride your toothpaste just left behind, cutting its cavity protection short.
**Starting the day with an intense workout on no food** -> can spike cortisol higher than usual, which over months may leave you more fatigued, not less.

caption:
Let's talk about a few of these. Orange juice feels like the obvious healthy choice, but once it's squeezed and separated from the fiber of the whole fruit, your body absorbs that sugar almost as quickly as a sugary drink — the vitamin C is great, the glucose spike isn't. Your multivitamin is another sneaky one: vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, meaning they literally dissolve into fat to be carried into your bloodstream, so popping them with just water and no food can mean you're flushing a chunk of that pill away. And mouthwash — rinsing right after brushing washes off the concentrated fluoride layer your toothpaste left behind, before it's had time to actually strengthen your enamel. None of this means ditch the habit, just shift the timing. Everyone's body is different, listen to yours.
